Team —

Putting together the weekly "capacity mosaic" to lock in GPU windows for the next 8 weeks. Primary objectives: protect committed slots for pending deals, identify where we can offer burst or alternate options, and surface any infra constraints before we push closes into a calendar week.

Attached: capacity_mosaic_v1.xlsx (tabbed by week, deal, committed %). Please do the following by EOD Tuesday:

- Sales (Ben / Laura): confirm per-deal committed slot counts and likely close week (column C-E). Mark high-confidence deals with ✅.
- Infra (Logan / Rishi): flag weeks with maintenance, A/B hardware mismatches, and suggest immediate mitigations (burst credits, pre-warm, quantized variants).
- Finance (Mina): call out billing cadence constraints or invoicing preferences that affect whether we ask for upfront reserved commits.

Specifically call out Acme Health (DEAL-7821) — they indicated a tentatively committed pilot the week of Sep 13. If that stays, we need to reserve 12 A100 slots + 4 burst H100 windows for load testing.

Quick ask: add your rows directly in the sheet and leave a one-line summary in reply so I can circulate an updated plan to the customer on Thursday.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ask. Two quick finance points:

1) Billing cadence: if a customer wants reserved capacity with a discount ladder, we should be explicit about when the invoice hits (upfront vs monthly amortization). For ACME, if they want promotional burst credits, we prefer the reserved ladder with 50% upfront and monthly amortization.
2) Credit exposure: Acme's procurement has a standard net-45; given this is a pilot with burst, ask for a P.O. to lock the commitment. I'll attach a small modeling doc that shows cash flow impact for a 6-month ladder vs payg + burst.

Attaching: nimble_burst_modeling.pdf

Please note: finance needs the final committed slot counts before Thursday to finalize invoice timing.

—Mina

Subject: Re: Capacity mosaic: weekly deal-tiling plan for upcoming closes

Looping infra constraints and mitigations:

- Week of Sep 13 (Acme tentative): We have scheduled firmware maintenance on ~30% of the A100 pool on Sep 10-12 for host kernel upgrades. That reduces usable A100 slots that week.
- Immediate mitigations:
  • Offer Acme a hybrid: 8 A100 reserved + 4 burst H100 windows (H100 available but needs extra quota request).
  • Pre-warm plan: we can bring up ephemeral burst nodes 48 hours before test window — incurs 15% higher cost but keeps latency stable.
  • Quantized model variant: recommend the <model>-q4 variant for load tests — reduces token cost and allows more sessions per GPU. Redwood Optimize suggests ~1.6x throughput on A100 for that variant.

Action items for infra: I'll add a column in the sheet marking weeks with maintenance risk and proposed mitigation. If sales want hard guarantees, we need an explicit reserved commit (we can offer a short-term SLA for reserved slots on a paid ladder).

—Logan
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes to add:

- If Acme will accept a quantized variant for load tests, we should compile and validate the q4f16 path on H100 before the test week; compile time ~6 hrs per model, can run in parallel.
- Alternative: spin up smaller A100 instances with continuous batching to soak traffic during peak test hours. That reduces per-token cost and smooths KV cache pressure.
- I'll put together a short runbook (build + warm + failover) and link it in the drive folder. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.
